title: Batching & Caching Concierge: SLO-envelope driven recommendations and safe applies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight 'Concierge' service that generates per-route batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations that are constrained by a latency/throughput SLO envelope and that can be safely applied with automated shadow-canary and deterministic rollback. This ticket implements the decision surface, application flow, and safety gates required for initial rollout to non-critical routes.

Why: Current Optimize suggestions reduce token cost but occasionally increase tail latency or reduce throughput under bursty traffic. We need an automated recommendations pipeline that reasons about SLO risk, simulates impact on real traffic (shadow apply), and provides a safe, auditable apply/rollback path for production.

Scope:
- Recommendation engine component that reads recent per-route histograms, KV cache hit-rate, and batching profile and emits a ranked set of candidate config changes (batch window, max batch size, cache TTL/keys to cache).
- SLO-envelope evaluator: computes predicted latency/throughput delta and a risk score using a sliding-window latency envelope + capacity headroom model.
- Safe-apply flow: runway stage (dry-run -> shadow canary -> staged traffic ramp -> monitor & auto-rollback) with automatic safeguards (throughput escrow limiter, latency envelope guard, anomaly detector).
- Console UI hooks (Optimize) to preview recommendation, view simulation, and approve/abort apply.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts for canary and post-apply regression signals.

Out of scope: deep model quantization tuning, dedicated GPU pool autoscaler changes.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces candidate config set for 95% of inspected routes within 5m of request and includes predicted median and P95 latency impact.
Shadow-canary flow can proxy 1% of production traffic and keep it isolated with no customer-visible degradation.
Automated rollback triggers when P95 latency increases by >20% over baseline or error rate increases by >2x during canary/staged apply.
Console shows simulation results, risk score, and an audit trail for every apply/rollback attempt.
End-to-end integration test that performs shadow-apply on synthetic bursty traffic and results in no more than 5% request failure inflation compared to baseline.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Data contracts - finalize metrics schema (per-route histograms, kv hit-rate, batch size distribution), add missing tags to traces.
Week 2: Build recommendation engine prototype (statistical heuristics + conservative defaults), SLO-envelope evaluator in service 'concierge-recommender'.
Week 3: Implement shadow-canary proxy, traffic isolation (via feature-flag and routing policy) and escrow limiter for throughput headroom.
Week 4: Integrate anomaly detector (probabilistic change-point + rolling z-score on P95) and automatic rollback controller with hysteresis windows.
Week 5: Console integration, UX preview & approve flow, and dashboards. End-to-end QA on staging.
observability_signatures: per-route median, P95, P99 latency (client-observed + server processing) pre/during/post apply
throughput (RPS) and useful token throughput comparison
batch size distribution and average batch latency
KV cache hit/miss rate and cache eviction churn
error rate (5xx) and application-level error signals
trace tail latency percentiles and 95th-ms distribution delta
rollback_conditions: P95 latency > baseline * 1.20 for a sustained 3-minute window during canary or ramp
Request error rate increased by >= 2x for a sustained 2-minute window
Throughput drops by > 30% while upstream SLOs (success rate) not improving
Anomaly detector reports a statistically significant change-point (p < 0.01) in latency distribution
Manual abort by oncall or PM with documented reason in audit trail
qa_plan: Create synthetic traffic generator that can reproduce prefix caching scenarios and bursty arrival patterns; run baseline + recommended config in parallel (shadow).
Run A/B style tests in staging with canary ramping (1% -> 5% -> 20%) and validate rollback triggers activate under injected regressions.
Load test: 2x normal peak for 30 minutes to validate throughput escrow behaves and does not starve critical routes.
Security review of config apply API (authz) and KMS usage for any sensitive telemetry; ensure RBAC checks in private deployments.
notes_and_decisions: Decision: Start with conservative heuristic model rather than ML model to reduce risk in initial rollout. ML-based candidate ranking is in backlog for Q3 2026.
Decision: Use 'latency envelope' approach (sliding-window percentiles + capacity buffer) rather than instantaneous threshold to tolerate short spikes.
Implementation note: escrow limiter holds a fraction of server capacity as 'burst credit' to ensure staged applies do not consume headroom needed by latency-sensitive routes.
Trade-off: Conservative defaults may under-capture cost savings initially; acceptable to favor SLO preservation for first shipping iteration.

2026-03-02 Diego Ramos: Prototype recommender emits candidates with predicted P50/P95 deltas; initial risk score calibrated against last 30 days of traffic. See confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPT/pages/Batching+Concierge+Design
2026-03-05 Engineering review: Agreed to shadow-canary first, then staged apply with 10-minute hold windows. Security flagged feature-flag gating for private deployments.
2026-03-08 QA: Synthetic burst tests show the escrow limiter prevents P95 degradation in 90% of cases; two routes still regressed — added route-level exclusion list.
